## Driver loop and accepted steps (`integration:`) {#sec-ch01-driver}

### Summary

A snapy block does not step itself. The program that owns it, the driver, runs the time loop. It asks the block for a
safe time step and calls every stage of the integrator. It then asks whether the step must be redone, and writes the
outputs of an accepted step. This section shows that loop as the two shipped examples run it, so a reader can write a
driver of their own or follow an existing one.

**One time step, in order.** (1) `max_time_step` picks $\Delta t$[^rg-473f42b9b5af]. (2) Each stage of the integrator runs
`MeshBlockImpl::advance_local`, which reconstructs the face states, solves the Riemann problems, limits the fluxes and
forms their divergence, adds the forcings and the vertical implicit correction, applies the user stage forcings, takes
the RK[^rg-251dacab968c] average with the conserved limiter, refills the solids, adjusts the phases and the gravity work on the last
stage only, and fills the physical ghosts; @sec-ch02-laws lists these six steps with their owners. (3) `run_hydro`
alone then runs the kinetics step. (4) `check_redo` accepts, redoes or stops. (5) On acceptance the clock advances and
`make_outputs` writes. The Code layer below gives the anchors of (1), (3), (4) and (5)
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}} for (2)).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: choose the step, run the stages, accept or redo, write outputs.

**Data.** In: a block or mesh and the integration limits. Out: outputs of accepted steps and the exit status.

**Placement.** The outermost loop: `max_time_step`, the stages, `check_redo`, `make_outputs`, `finalize`.

**Activation.** Caller supplied; the integration defaults belong to pyharp.

**Guarantee / limits.** A map, no order; the example runs kinetics after the stages and before `check_redo`.

**Evidence.** `test_check_redo_parallel.<b>` (exact) and `test_restart_cycle_limit`; see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $n_{\mathrm{redo}}$ is the number of redos of the current step (`current_redo`);
$\Delta t_{\mathrm{bound}}$ is the block's local step bound before the Courant number $C$[^rg-25ec79df3164] (`cfl`[^rg-d9e768dc5199], @sec-ch07) is applied.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived in
their owning chapters. The loop's bookkeeping is checked on a port of the driver loop. A rejected step leaves the
clock and the cycle count where they were, and outputs follow only accepted steps [check
`src/snapy_report/ch01/checks/driver_check.py`, output `driver_check.out`, `[C1]`]. Each redo halves the step of the retry
(`[C2]`), and a negative `check_redo` ends the loop at the time of the last accepted step (`[C3]`).

### Numerical method

The driver keeps the clock unchanged when a step is rejected. A positive return from `check_redo` repeats the cycle
and a negative return ends it. Only after a zero return does the clock advance and `make_outputs` run.
`MeshBlockImpl::max_time_step` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::max_time_step >}}) takes the block's
local bound, reduces it with MIN across the process group. It returns that times the Courant number $C$ and $2^{-n_{\mathrm{redo}}}$, with
$n_{\mathrm{redo}}$ the number of redos of the current step. `make_outputs`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs >}}) accumulates statistics on every call and writes a
file when the clock has reached the output's next time; `finalize`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize >}}) forces a last write. The single-block example `main` of
{{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}} writes an initial output only on a fresh start, and applies the kinetics step
after all dynamics stages and before `check_redo`. The mesh example `main` of {{< code examples/straka.cpp main >}}
writes an initial output unconditionally, restart included. No spatial or temporal order belongs to this control flow;
it inherits the selected operators.

**Why the loop is safe to repeat.** Four facts of the code make a redo exact and an accepted step well defined. The
round-off that enters is bounded in step 3.

1. *A rejected step leaves the clock alone.* `++block->cycle` and `current_time += dt` run only after `check_redo`
   returned zero ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}), so a repeated or an ended step advances neither the
   cycle count nor the clock; `apply_redo` does not touch the cycle.
2. *A redo restores the saved state.* `apply_redo` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}})
   copies the step-start buffers back and increments `current_redo`, and the next `max_time_step` reads it.
3. *The halving is exact.* `max_time_step` returns $2^{-n_{\mathrm{redo}}}\,C\,\Delta t_{\mathrm{bound}}$. Multiplying
   a double by $2^{-n_{\mathrm{redo}}}$ changes only its exponent, so it is exact until underflow; the one product
   $C\,\Delta t_{\mathrm{bound}}$ is rounded once, with relative error at most
   $\delta_{\mathrm{mach}} = 2^{-53}$. The MIN reduction across ranks selects one of the operands and adds no error.
4. *Outputs follow accepted steps only.* `make_outputs` runs after the cycle and clock increments and writes when the
   clock has reached the output's next time ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs >}}).

: Implementation anchors for the driver loop. {#tbl-ch01-driver-code}

1. Choose the step: `max_time_step` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::max_time_step >}}).
2. Run every stage through `forward` (@sec-ch01-block-forward) and, in `run_hydro`, the kinetics step
   ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).
3. Decide: `check_redo` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::check_redo >}}) returns positive to
   repeat, negative to stop, zero to accept; `apply_redo` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}})
   counts the redo and restores the saved state.
4. Write: `make_outputs` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs >}}) after the accepted
   cycle and clock increments; `finalize` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize >}}) at the end.

**How to use it.** The driver reads the integration block of the card; the three snapy keys and the six
keys pyharp reads are the only ones accepted ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}):

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `integration`[^rg-63ada7768d37], `tlim`[^rg-955cd175eb5b], `nlim`[^rg-9702bd7116a5], `implicit-scheme`[^rg-04fd7cd8be70].
```yaml
integration:
  cfl: 0.9            # Courant number C of the time step
  tlim: 3600.0        # s; stop predicate of the integrator
  nlim: 100000        # cycle limit
  implicit-scheme: 0  # 0 explicit; 1 and 9 select the vertical implicit solves
```

**Not provided:** a safe range or a maximum for `cfl`; 0.9 is the value the code ships, not a measured stability
limit. The limit depends on the integrator (@sec-ch07-rk), the reconstruction and the Riemann solver (@sec-ch04)
together, and no test at the pin integrates a run at increasing $C$ to find where it fails. What $C$ multiplies is
in @sec-ch07-cfl.

Refused: any other key under `integration`, with its path in the error; `implicit-advection-cfl`[^rg-cb6cdb706a5c] or `shear-cfl`[^rg-be87d6fbf19d]
without `implicit-scheme`, because they bound an implicit direction that does not exist (@sec-ch12-yaml). A
driver of your own repeats the loop of `main` ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}):

```cpp
  while (!block->pintg->stop(block->cycle, current_time)) {
    auto dt = block->max_time_step(vars);
    block->print_cycle_info(vars, current_time, dt);

    // evolve dynamics
    for (int stage = 0; stage < block->pintg->stages.size(); ++stage) {
      block->forward(vars, dt, stage);
    }

    // evolve kinetics
    auto &hydro_u = vars["hydro_u"];
    auto &hydro_w = vars["hydro_w"];

    // Kinetics needs the final dynamics state, including saturation adjustment.
    peos->forward(hydro_u, hydro_w);
    auto temp = peos->compute("W->T", {hydro_w});
    auto pres = hydro_w[IPR];
    auto xfrac = thermo_y->compute("Y->X", {hydro_w.narrow(0, ICY, ny)});
    auto conc = thermo_x->compute("TPX->V", {temp, pres, xfrac});
    auto cp_vol = thermo_x->compute("TV->cp", {temp, conc});

    // auto conc_kinet = kinet->options.narrow_copy(conc, thermo_y->options);
    auto conc_kinet = conc.slice(-1, 1, conc.size(-1));
    auto [rate, rc_ddC, rc_ddT, rate_constants] =
        kinet->forward_with_rate_constants(temp, pres, conc_kinet);
    auto jac = kinet->jacobian(temp, conc_kinet, cp_vol, rate, rc_ddC, rc_ddT,
                               rate_constants);
    auto del_conc = kintera::evolve_implicit(rate, kinet->stoich, jac, dt);
    std::vector<int64_t> vec(del_conc.dim(), 1);
    vec[del_conc.dim() - 1] = -1;
    auto del_rho = del_conc / thermo_y->inv_mu.narrow(0, 1, ny).view(vec);
    hydro_u.narrow(0, ICY, ny) += del_rho.permute({3, 0, 1, 2});

    int err = block->check_redo(vars);
    if (err > 0) continue;  // redo this step with smaller dt
    if (err < 0) break;     // terminate simulation

    // make outputs
    ++block->cycle;
    current_time += dt;
    block->make_outputs(vars, current_time);
  }
```

The first two lines inside the loop are step 1 of the walk-through; `print_cycle_info` writes the cycle log of
@sec-ch13 and changes no state. The `for` loop is step 2. The kinetics block is the example's own chemistry update,
with kintera's implicit solver ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}). It is not part of the block API[^rg-12b6d47ad2b9]. It runs on
the state the stages left, before `check_redo`. The `check_redo` lines are step 3 and the last three lines step 4.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_check_redo_parallel.<b>` | one redo decision across two ranks; the rolled-back state equals the saved one | exact equality | saved tensors are copied back |
| `tests/run_restart_cycle_limit.py` (`test_restart_cycle_limit`) | the restarted run resumes at the matching cycle and ends at the same time | absolute $10^{-12}$ on logged values, $10^{-9}$ on the termination time | the script's `assert_close` |
| this chapter's check, `driver_check.py` | `[C1]`-`[C3]`: clock, step halving and stop, on a port of the loop | exact | logic port |

: Source assertions for the driver loop. {#tbl-ch01-driver-tests}

The parallel assertion is {{< code tests/test_check_redo_parallel.cpp Mesh.check_redo_is_one_decision_across_ranks >}};
the script's checks are `assert_close` ({{< code tests/run_restart_cycle_limit.py assert_close >}}) in `main`
({{< code tests/run_restart_cycle_limit.py main >}}), which exits with the skip code 125 when the driver
executable is not available. The ctest `test_restart_cycle_limit` runs it, registered with the other restart tests
({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}) on every platform but macOS.

The check is a port of the loop as a state machine driven by a scripted sequence of `check_redo`
results.[^ch01-driver-run] `[C1]`: a rejected step leaves the clock and the cycle count where they were. Outputs
follow only accepted steps (time 4.05 after accepted steps of 1.8, 0.45 and 1.8, cycle 3, four outputs). `[C2]`: each
redo halves the step of the retry (1.8, 0.9, 0.45, 0.225). `[C3]`: a negative `check_redo` ends the loop at the time
of the last accepted step (1.80 after three attempts, two outputs).

`test_restart_cycle_limit` passes at the pin.[^ch01-driver-restart] The two-rank ctest runs on CPU[^rg-8f99acfe5206] only and has not
been run for this report at the pin: **pending a pinned ctest run**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The restart writer saves the output counters as they stand when it runs, inside `make_outputs`; together with
the unconditional initial output of `straka`, this is a code-level reason to check for repeated restart
outputs, and no overwrite experiment is reported here. The kinetics step of `run_hydro` lives in the driver,
outside the block's stage.
:::
